title: Crossing the Jordan and Covenant Renewal

date.label: Undated Joshua narrative
date.note: Biblical narrative chronology is not independently established as an absolute BCE date.

claims.claim: The narrative places Gilgal on Jericho’s eastern edge after crossing (Joshua 4:19–20)
Israel crosses while ark-bearing priests stand in Jordan (Joshua 3:14–17)
Two twelve-stone references require literary examination (Joshua 4:3–9,20)
Circumcision and Passover are narrated after crossing (Joshua 5:2–12)

connections.note: The earlier crossing of the sea supplies the central literary analogue for the crossing of the Jordan, although the two events are distinct.
The command of circumcision in Genesis 17 provides the background for the renewal of circumcision in Joshua 5.
The institution of Passover in Exodus 12 clarifies the observance of Passover in Joshua 5.
The directives for inscribed stones and an altar after the crossing invite textual comparison with Joshua 3–4, without identifying the two monuments.
The later Jordan-crossing episode in 2 Kings 2 uses the same miracle motif, but it is not the same historical occurrence.
